newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to make pay offer, fears worker action.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to make pay offer, fears worker action.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said it would later on Thursday be issuing a wage offer to its administrative employees in a bid to avert what it saw as possible industrial action by them.

A spokesman for the DAG white-collar union, with which Lufthansa is negotiating, confirmed that it was expecting to receive the offer from Lufthansa by 1600 GMT but would not comment on future action if it was considered insufficient.

Lufthansa, which last month struck a two-year pay deal with 50,000 workers represented by the OeTV public sector and transport union, said it would in any case be able to cope with industrial action if it took place.
"All Lufthansa passangers can safely assume that preparations will be made so that flights can continue as normal," the airline said in a statement.
DAG, which is seeking a four percent rise in wages for its members next year, has said that Lufthansa offers up till now would leave them with a pay rise below inflation.
